vuln_id: OSS-Fuzz issue 64570 / ARVO arvo:64570 / wolfMQTT CONNECT_ACK stale props wild write
classification_note: The reproduced sanitizer symptom is a SEGV caused by a write in `MqttProps_Free`, but the source-level defect is earlier: the shared `client->msg` union is reused as a `MqttConnectAck` without a guaranteed reset, and vulnerable CONNECT_ACK decoding does not unconditionally clear `connect_ack->props` before cleanup later treats that stale pointer field as a valid `MqttProp` list head.

bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged PoC / vulnerable source from gt-arvo_64570-workspace
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer crash with the exact staged 146-byte libFuzzer datasource saved as `poc` (SHA-256 `e09db34661a0c99e94b76b5a1dc89f88cbf7370e44c177af6e28e7d7357c10be`). The staged harness zeros `client` directly instead of calling `MqttClient_Init()`, `MqttSocket_Init()` only installs network callbacks, and `MqttClient_Connect()` copies `client->protocol_level` into the outbound CONNECT request rather than initializing the client from it. On the crashing call, the saved `MqttClient_WaitType:1296 -> MqttClient_HandlePacket:851` frames are source-consistent only if `wolfMQTTFuzzer::wait()` reaches `MqttClient_WaitMessage_ex(client, &client->msg, ...)` while `client->msg.stat.read` is already `MQTT_MSG_PAYLOAD`, so the header-read path at `MqttClient_WaitType:1193-1201` does not run and `MqttClient_PacketReset(packet_type, &client->msg)` does not clear the shared union object. In that payload-resume case the local `packet_type` stays `MQTT_PACKET_TYPE_RESERVED`, `use_packet_obj` remains the non-NULL `&client->msg`, and lines 1278-1284 force the outer call through `MqttClient_HandlePacket`'s PUBLISH arm at line 851. While that outer state machine is still on the PUBLISH payload path, the inner `MqttClient_DecodePacket` first parses the current buffered bytes and selects CONNECT_ACK. Because the CONNECT_ACK arm reuses the uncleared shared object, skips the zeroing path for the local temporary, and refreshes only `p_connect_ack->protocol_level = client->protocol_level` before decode, the `props` slot can retain stale union contents. Vulnerable `MqttDecode_ConnectAck()` never unconditionally clears `connect_ack->props`, and `MqttClient_DecodePacket()` immediately forwards the returned `p_connect_ack->props` value into `Handle_Props(..., 1)`. `Handle_Props()` then calls `MqttProps_Free()`, which writes through `head->type = MQTT_PROP_NONE` and produces the reproduced wild-address WRITE at `0x202020202028`. The staged fix closes this obligation by adding `connect_ack->props = 0;` before optional CONNECT_ACK property handling, alongside analogous zeroing in related response decoders.

source.description: First project-side parse of the current crashing buffered bytes inside the inner decode that runs while the outer state machine is still on the resumed PUBLISH payload path. The header nibble from attacker-controlled `rx_buf` selects which overlay of the reused shared packet object is consumed.
source.value_from: The staged witness is the exact 146-byte file `gt_results/arvo_64570/poc` with SHA-256 `e09db34661a0c99e94b76b5a1dc89f88cbf7370e44c177af6e28e7d7357c10be`. On the crashing inner decode, the header byte consumed here resolves to `MQTT_PACKET_TYPE_CONNECT_ACK`; that is fixed by the reproduced ASan frame at `MqttClient_DecodePacket /src/wolfmqtt/src/mqtt_client.c:593`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled first header byte materializes as `packet_type` here. That dispatch value selects the CONNECT_ACK decoder arm that reinterprets the reused shared `client->msg` object.
tainted_value_origin.note: The reproduced `MqttClient_DecodePacket:593` frame fixes that the crashing inner decode took the CONNECT_ACK case selected here.

root_cause.description: The CONNECT_ACK decoder updates `flags` and `return_code`, but vulnerable source never performs an unconditional `connect_ack->props = 0` before optional property parsing. On a reused `MqttConnectAck` overlay, that omission lets the stale `props` field survive into cleanup.
root_cause.note: The fixing hunk adds `connect_ack->props = 0;` immediately before the conditional property handling. The saved artifacts do not establish whether that v5 property block executed on the crashing run; they only establish that the decoder returned with stale `connect_ack->props` still live.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The property cleanup routine treats the stale `props` value as a valid `MqttProp*` and writes through it.
sink.note: The reproduced run reports `AddressSanitizer: SEGV` caused by a WRITE at `/src/wolfmqtt/src/mqtt_packet.c:1902:20` with wild address `0x202020202028`.

payload_resume_path.description: The saved frames `MqttClient_WaitType:1296` and `MqttClient_HandlePacket:851` are source-consistent only when this call enters the payload-resume case with `client->msg.stat.read` already at `MQTT_MSG_PAYLOAD` or `MQTT_MSG_PAYLOAD2`. In that case the earlier header path at lines 1194-1201, including `MqttClient_PacketReset(packet_type, &client->msg)`, does not execute on the crashing call.

parser_admitted.description: The reproduced ASan frame at line 593 proves that the inner decode selected the CONNECT_ACK arm while reinterpreting the reused shared packet object.

evidence_limitations: The public OSS-Fuzz issue text labels the bug `UNKNOWN READ`, but the reproduced Stage 01 sanitizer trace is a WRITE at `MqttProps_Free:1902`. The issue match is grounded on the identical project stack `MqttProps_Free -> Handle_Props -> MqttClient_DecodePacket`.

Runtime disambiguation is disabled for this sample (`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false), so the reused-state fact represented by the outer `MqttClient_HandlePacket:851` frame is closed by source reasoning from the saved line-number combination rather than by a fresh instrumented run.

The saved artifacts do not preserve which earlier event left `client->msg.stat.read` in `MQTT_MSG_PAYLOAD`, which stale union bytes occupied `client->msg`, or what value `client->protocol_level` held when step 3 copied it into `p_connect_ack->protocol_level`. Because the harness never calls `MqttClient_Init()` and runtime disambiguation is disabled, this trace does not claim which optional CONNECT_ACK property-parsing branch ran; it stays at the proved obligation that the crashing call skipped `MqttClient_PacketReset`, reused a non-NULL shared packet object, and reached `Handle_Props` with a stale `connect_ack->props` field that vulnerable source had not unconditionally cleared.

fine_trace.note: The crashing call comes from `MqttClient_WaitMessage_ex(client, &client->msg, ...)`, so `packet_obj` is the shared `&client->msg`. The saved `MqttClient_WaitType:1296 -> MqttClient_HandlePacket:851` line combination is source-consistent only if this invocation enters with `mms_stat->read` already at `MQTT_MSG_PAYLOAD`, which skips the earlier header path at lines 1194-1201 and therefore skips `MqttClient_PacketReset(packet_type, &client->msg)`. Local `packet_type` then stays at its initialized `MQTT_PACKET_TYPE_RESERVED`, `use_packet_obj` remains the non-NULL shared object, and lines 1278-1284 force outer handling through the PUBLISH arm without clearing the union storage.

Source. While the outer state machine is still on the forced PUBLISH payload path from step 1, the current attacker-controlled bytes in `client->rx_buf` are first parsed here by the inner decode, and the header nibble selects the decoder arm. On the crashing path, ASAN's next project frame at line 593 proves that this packet type resolves to `MQTT_PACKET_TYPE_CONNECT_ACK`.

Because step 1 supplied a non-NULL shared `packet_obj`, the CONNECT_ACK arm reuses `client->msg` storage instead of the zeroed local `connect_ack` temporary. The else zeroing path is skipped; before decode the only field this arm refreshes is `p_connect_ack->protocol_level = client->protocol_level`, so the reused union object's `props` slot is not cleared here.

Root cause. Vulnerable CONNECT_ACK decoding refreshes `flags` and `return_code`, but there is no unconditional `connect_ack->props = 0` before any optional property parsing. The saved artifacts do not establish whether the `connect_ack->protocol_level >= MQTT_CONNECT_PROTOCOL_LEVEL_5` block executed on the crashing run; what they do establish is that the function returned without clearing the reused `connect_ack->props` field, so the stale pointer from step 3 survived into step 5. The staged fix adds that missing zeroing here.

Since the CONNECT_ACK decode returned `rc >= 0` and `doProps` is true on this path, `MqttClient_DecodePacket` immediately forwards whatever `p_connect_ack->props` still contains into `Handle_Props` before nulling the field. On the crashing run that value is the stale non-NULL pointer carried through steps 3-4.

The stale pointer from step 5 is non-NULL, so `Handle_Props` enters its `props != NULL` block. Because CONNECT_ACK passed `free_props = 1`, cleanup forwards that stale value into `MqttProps_Free` instead of ignoring it.

Sink. `MqttProps_Free` trusts `head` as a valid `MqttProp*` and writes `head->type = MQTT_PROP_NONE` before following `head->next`. On the reproduced run ASAN reports that first write as a SEGV on wild address `0x202020202028`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds the missing `connect_ack->props = 0;` and similar initialization in related decoders, but Stage 02 did not run a fixed build; `patch_resolves` therefore remains false here.

cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: The fine trace matches the reproduced project frames `MqttProps_Free:1902`, `Handle_Props:527`, and `MqttClient_DecodePacket:593`; the outer frames `MqttClient_HandlePacket:851`, `MqttClient_WaitType:1296`, and `MqttClient_WaitMessage_ex:2708` are represented by the payload-resume transition in fine_trace step 1.

poc.trigger: The exact staged 146-byte libFuzzer datasource witness (SHA-256 `e09db34661a0c99e94b76b5a1dc89f88cbf7370e44c177af6e28e7d7357c10be`) drives `wolfMQTTFuzzer::Run()` into `wait()`, after which the saved run reaches `MqttClient_WaitMessage()` and crashes in `MqttProps_Free` on this same file.

format.name: libFuzzer datasource for wolfmqtt-fuzzer
format.contract: Exactly the staged `poc` file. The verified trigger is not generalized beyond this witness: it must preserve the message-state evolution that reuses `client->msg`, must reach the CONNECT_ACK arm on that reused object, and must return from decode with a stale non-NULL `connect_ack->props` value that is forwarded into cleanup.
